headline: ILLEGAL BLOCKADE Halts Orla's Camino Rojo Mine — Shares Plunge 8% as Equinox Merger Hangs
snippet: Unionized workers imposed an illegal work stoppage and blockade at Orla Mining's Camino Rojo gold mine in Zacatecas, Mexico on June 1, halting all operations in a dispute over productivity bonuses and profit-sharing payments (PTU). Shares fell nearly 8% on the news, with a federal conciliation meeting scheduled for June 2 — adding operational risk to the pending $18.5B all-share merger with Equinox Gold.

headline: IAMGOLD Lifts Côté Gold to 20.3 Million Ounces — 12% Jump on Gosselin Integration
snippet: IAMGOLD released an updated mineral resource for the Côté Gold Mine in northeastern Ontario on June 1, upgrading M&I resources to 20.34 million oz (+12%) after integrating the Gosselin zone into a consolidated block model. Inferred resources surged 61% to 3.48 million oz; a full expansion study and updated mine plan is expected in Q4 2026.

headline: Americas Gold & Silver Returns 599 g/t Ag at Cosalá — More Than 5X Over Modeled Resource
snippet: Americas Gold and Silver released infill drill results from the Cosalá Complex in Sinaloa, Mexico on June 1, with best hole SR568 returning 14.0m at 599.8 g/t silver — over five times the modeled resource grade in that section. Conversion drilling across three zones is running 2–3x modeled grades, signalling a material resource upgrade ahead of an optimized H2 2026 mine plan.

headline: Pan American Silver Commits $146M to Timmins Shaft Deepening and Two New Ontario Deposits
snippet: Pan American Silver's board approved Phase 1 of the Timmins Camp Project on June 1 — a C$201M ($146M USD) program to deepen the Bell Creek mine shaft and drive development drifts to the Vogel and Samson satellite deposits, extending mine life at its flagship Ontario silver operation following a multi-year exploration success.

headline: COPPER SURGES TO $6.56/LB — Chile Posts Weakest April Output in 23 Years
snippet: Copper futures hit $6.56/lb on June 2, up 0.57% on the day and 13.2% over the past month, as Chile's Cochilco reported April production of roughly 400,000 tonnes — the country's weakest monthly output in 23 years. AI data centre construction and power-grid electrification demand continue to underpin the bull case for the red metal.

headline: Ghana Activates 30% Gold Mandate at Large Mines on June 1, Bolstering Central Bank Reserves
snippet: Ghana's central bank began purchasing 30% of doré output from large-scale gold producers on June 1, up from 20%, to build gold reserves and support local refining capacity. Miners are reportedly still negotiating the 0.6% pricing discount, with the Ghana Chamber of Mines saying final commercial terms are not yet settled.

headline: Gold Holds at $4,517 as Analyst Forecasts Split: JPMorgan Eyes $5,055 Q4 While Bears Watch $4,500
snippet: Gold spot traded at $4,517/oz on June 1 — a $78 drop in a single session — as analysts diverge sharply on the June outlook. JPMorgan maintains a $5,055/oz Q4 target, a Reuters poll of 31 analysts sees a $4,916 median, while technical analysts are watching for a potential break below the $4,500 psychological floor amid a stronger dollar and cooling geopolitical premium.

headline: Silver Holds Above $75 as Structural Deficit Enters Fifth Consecutive Year
snippet: Silver traded at $75.53/oz on June 1 — up more than $40 over the past year — supported by the Silver Institute's confirmation of a 2025 supply deficit of 148.9 million oz, the market's fourth consecutive annual shortfall. Stalled US-Iran ceasefire negotiations kept oil-linked inflation expectations elevated, adding a monetary bid to existing industrial demand for the metal.

headline: After Record Q1 Profits, Gold Miners Face Q2 Diesel Shock — Remote Open Pits Most Exposed
snippet: Q1 2026 peaked for gold producers — Newmont posted $3.3B in free cash flow and Agnico Eagle achieved a $2,800/oz operating margin — but analysts now warn Q2 faces a dual headwind: gold prices down from their $4,900 Q1 average, and refined diesel up 50–100% in key jurisdictions due to Hormuz shipping disruptions. Remote open-pit operations with no grid connection carry 30–40% cost exposure.

headline: Alaska Silver Mobilizes Two Rigs for 6,000m Drill at Illinois Creek — Silver Sage Zone Targets Start
snippet: Alaska Silver Corp. launched a fully-funded 6,000m summer drill program at its 32,737-hectare Illinois Creek silver-gold-lead-zinc project in western Alaska, with two company-owned rigs now active. Priority targets include the Waterpump Creek deposit and the newly discovered Silver Sage Zone — a 550m-long breccia trend that returned up to 1,235 g/t silver in 2025 surface trenching.
